clue.text: Attempt a portion of beef for two

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tries to serve a shared helping of beef for two diners.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a try at doing something, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Resident abroad subsequently heading off round Pennsylvania

indicators.note: round says the shortened word is placed around the state abbreviation
heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: next means afterwards, subsequently
PA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: Someone living overseas later sets out on a trip around Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter of the synonym, and 'round' wraps what is left around the state's postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for expatriate, someone who lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Genuine article installed by company as warning device

indicators.note: installed by says one piece is fitted inside the word for company

parts.note: a firm is a business company
real means genuine
a is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: An authentic item fitted by a business serves as an alarm unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed by' means fitted inside: the genuine article goes into the company after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a device that sounds to alert people to a blaze.

clue.text: Supremes singer, one entertaining trendy musician

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting, holding a guest within

parts.note: Diana Ross was lead singer of the Supremes
one is the Roman numeral I
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A Motown star hosts a fashionable fellow performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Ross fronted the 1960s Motown group the Supremes; 'entertaining' has her plus the numeral hosting the trendy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian opera composer, a classical musician.

clue.text: Helpful type, like close relative

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a sister is a close family relative

explanation.surface: A helpful person is described as being like a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assists is a helper, a helpful type of person.

clue.text: Teach-sir dot com revolutionised the education system

indicators.note: revolutionised means completely changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A website promising teachers a radical overhaul of the schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The Socratic method is a way of teaching by question and answer, a classroom approach named after an ancient philosopher.

clue.text: One part of the Bible- Old Testament book, actually

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
NT is the New Testament, one part of the Bible
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A remark that one section of scripture really is an Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning really or in fact.

clue.text: Giant container not quite big enough for storing it

indicators.note: storing says the shortened word holds the other piece inside it
not quite big enough says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a tank is a large container for liquid

explanation.surface: A huge container turns out to be slightly too small to store something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite big enough' drops the container's last letter, and 'storing' puts IT inside; 'for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of huge size, from the race of giant gods in Greek myth.

clue.text: More than one scripture teacher N makes sound R S improvements?

parts.note: RE is religious education, school scripture lessons
a master is a schoolteacher; 'More than one' makes it plural

explanation.surface: Several religious studies teachers seem to be getting better at acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one' asks for the plural of the teacher word.
explanation.definitionFit: Remastering an old recording improves its audio quality.

clue.text: String of high grades given to TV newslady, honest

parts.note: straight As is a run of top marks
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC television news reporter

explanation.surface: A newsreader is rewarded with top marks for being truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Adie was the BBC's chief news correspondent, famous in Britain for reporting from war zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight as a die is an idiom for completely truthful and upright.

clue.text: Patricia's terribly dependent on others

indicators.note: terribly suggests the name's letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: the name with its S, all as fodder

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be awfully reliant on other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off a host, so a parasitic person sponges on others.

clue.text: Art of piano playing?

parts.note: read 'Art' as a first name: the jazz pianist called Art, rather than the skill of playing

explanation.surface: A question about the skill of playing the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was an American jazz pianist celebrated for his virtuosity.

clue.text: Worker returns carrying garment for empress

indicators.note: carrying says the reversed word holds the garment inside
returns says the word for worker is written backwards

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
a sari is a garment worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: A labourer comes back holding a robe fit for a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' makes TNA, and 'carrying' has it hold the Indian garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar, an empress.

clue.text: Ex-student starts to make notes, getting in usual mess

indicators.note: getting in says those letters are put inside the jumbled word
mess means a muddle, so the letters are scrambled
starts to says take the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A former pupil begins jotting things down amid the usual chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' scrambles USUAL to ALUUS, and 'getting in' puts M and N (from 'starts to') in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former pupil or graduate of a school or college.

clue.text: Taking risks, as a pyromaniac may be?

explanation.surface: A fire-raiser is described as a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing something dangerous; literally, someone obsessed with starting blazes toys with flames.

clue.text: Musical piece making clergyman bitter?

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of a church
bitter is a kind of British beer, an ale

explanation.surface: A tune that sours a vicar's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like an adjective but is the British pub beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is an instrumental composition evoking rural life.

clue.text: Religious woman I first invited out is D E overwhelmed

parts.note: a nun is a woman in a religious order
to have dated someone is to have asked them out

explanation.surface: A man confesses he asked a nun on a date and is swamped by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the I before the religious woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated literally means flooded, and figuratively swamped, overwhelmed.

clue.text: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder?

definitions.text: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder?

parts.words: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder?
parts.note: the rock singer's famous song title read as a gloom that comes with one season of the year

explanation.surface: A rock'n'roll star suffers from winter depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasonal affective disorder usually strikes in winter, so a hot-season version is the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Cochran's 1958 rock hit was about the frustrations of a teenager in the holidays.

clue.text: Football team leaping over net

indicators.note: leaping suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer's shot sails over the goal net.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League club from Liverpool.

clue.text: Nationality is given during birth, possibly

indicators.note: given during says the short word is placed inside the other
possibly says the word's letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Citizenship is granted at the moment of being born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters into BRITH, and 'given during' puts the short word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being from Britain is a nationality.

clue.text: Bully journalists at work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Reporters at their jobs are accused of intimidation.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to treat harshly, to tyrannise.

clue.text: Pen used by American writer

explanation.surface: An enclosure is borrowed by a US author.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an animal enclosure; Ezra Pound was an American poet.

clue.text: Editor's repaired valves

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the word with its S, all as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone at the newspaper has fixed the radio's electronic components.
explanation.definitionFit: Triodes are thermionic tubes with three electrodes, known in Britain as valves.

clue.text: Tomatoes can be a bit off

explanation.surface: Tomatoes may be slightly past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of pips describes tomatoes; shabby or slightly unwell is the other sense.

clue.text: Grown-up: one having endlessly boring time

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: dull means boring

explanation.surface: A grown-up is someone having an endlessly tedious time.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a fully grown person.

clue.text: Shaw character idle, do you say?

indicators.note: do you say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to do little is to be idle

explanation.surface: A question about whether a character in a Shaw play is lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza and Alfred Doolittle are characters in George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion.

clue.text: Risk way to bring about appeasement

explanation.surface: A gamble taken to make peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is read as two words, a way of calming someone: stop their fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in danger is to risk; ending someone's wrath placates them.

clue.text: Reluctant to pen unconventional yarn

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so one word holds the other

parts.note: shy means reluctant, unwilling
odd means unconventional, strange

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to write about an unusual story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale but is wool: shoddy is yarn made from recycled rags.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cheap fibre made by shredding old woollen cloth.
